stem.text: An alkene reacts with hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ to produce a single organic product as shown.

stem.alt: Reaction scheme: alkene, with arrow labelled hot concentrated acidified KMnO4(aq), giving a single organic product drawn as a skeletal formula with a ketone C=O, a methyl branch and a terminal carboxylic acid (COOH).

stem.text: What is the structure of the alkene?

A.alt: Skeletal formula: a six-membered ring with a C=C; a methyl on one alkene carbon and a methyl on the ring carbon at the bottom.

B.alt: Skeletal formula: a six-membered ring with a C=C; a methyl on one alkene carbon and a methyl on the adjacent sp3 ring carbon.

C.alt: Skeletal formula: a five-membered ring with a C=C; a methyl on the alkene carbon at the top and a methyl on the sp3 carbon at the bottom-left.

D.alt: Skeletal formula: a five-membered ring with a C=C; a methyl on the alkene carbon at the top and a methyl on the adjacent sp3 carbon to the right.
